title: CoreDNS service IP times out while direct pod IPs and NodeLocal DNS work
body: I deployed Kubernetes 1.25.6 with Kubespray v2.21.0, Calico, CoreDNS, and NodeLocal DNS. CoreDNS 1.9.3 forwards external queries to /etc/resolv.conf, which initially lists both 169.254.25.10 for NodeLocal DNS and 10.30.1.1 for my network DNS. Queries sent directly to CoreDNS pod IPs work from every node, but queries to the CoreDNS service IP 10.133.0.3 succeed from only one node and time out from the others. Queries through 169.254.25.10 work. NodeLocal DNS continuously logs timeouts connecting to 10.133.0.3:53. From a NodeLocal DNS debug pod, a UDP query to 10.133.0.3 times out, while the same query over TCP succeeds. Across the nodes, UDP queries to the service IP fail everywhere, and TCP works everywhere except one node. Netchecker also reports one host-network agent as failing, and a request on its node takes about one minute.

symptoms_visible: I can resolve cluster records through each CoreDNS pod IP and through 169.254.25.10, but queries through the CoreDNS service IP 10.133.0.3 time out from most nodes.
UDP queries to 10.133.0.3 fail from every node; TCP works from all but one node.
My NodeLocal DNS pods continuously log i/o timeouts to 10.133.0.3:53, and netchecker takes about one minute on one host.
N0.label: N0 DNS service-path timeouts reported

symptoms_visible: The service-IP timeouts also occur in a separate cluster I deployed with Cilium.
My kubelet logs say the network plugin is not initialized, and Calico components log context-deadline timeouts when connecting to the Kubernetes service.
N1.label: N1 broader service networking evidence collected

symptoms_visible: After removing 169.254.25.10 from systemd-resolved and restarting the relevant services and pods, the NodeLocal DNS pods receive the correct resolv.conf, but they still log timeouts reaching 10.133.0.3:53.
N2_x.label: N2_x forwarding-loop cleanup aftermath

symptoms_visible: After setting Felix chainInsertMode to Append, I can access the CoreDNS service from every node and the NodeLocal DNS iptables rules remain present, but the DNS timeout errors continue.
Most uncached domain queries time out with a two-second limit but succeed when I allow five seconds.
N3_x.label: N3_x iptables adjustment aftermath

symptoms_visible: After disabling RX and TX offload on vxlan.calico, the DNS and one-minute timeout problem disappears immediately.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Since direct pod IPs work but service IPs time out, do the kubelet logs report any CNI or network-plugin errors?
Can you check the kubelet logs on an affected node for network readiness errors?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I checked the kubelet logs and found: "Container runtime network notready" with "NetworkPluginNotReady" and "cni plugin not initialized".

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The kubelet reports NetworkReady=true on every node, with no CNI initialization or service-network errors.
I see the same NetworkPluginNotReady line on two affected nodes instead of one.

question_patterns: Do the Calico components show connectivity failures to Kubernetes service addresses?
Can you check the Calico controller logs for API-service timeouts?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The Calico controller repeatedly logs context deadline exceeded while requesting https://10.133.0.1:443, including failures to read cluster information and the API server health endpoint.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Calico can consistently reach 10.133.0.1:443, and its logs contain no API-service timeouts.

edges.comment: From c9-c10 on the reporter's cluster: participant1 redirected attention from CoreDNS toward service networking, and the reporter supplied raw kubelet and Calico timeout lines. The separate Cilium deployment is an unprompted reporter observation folded into the target node.

solution.intent: Remove the NodeLocal DNS address from the host resolver inputs used as upstream servers, eliminating the forwarding loop, then restart systemd-resolved, kubelet, CoreDNS, and NodeLocal DNS so they reread the resolver configuration.
solution.concrete_example: Remove 169.254.25.10 from /etc/systemd/resolved.conf and ensure the resolver file selected by kubelet contains only genuine upstream DNS servers; reload systemd-resolved and recreate the DNS pods.

edges.comment: From c3-c8 on the reporter's nodes: the resolver configuration created a real partial forwarding loop, confirmed by the reporter's plugin/loop fatal line. Removing it corrected the pods' resolv.conf but did not eliminate the service-IP timeout problem, so it is a falsified complete resolution rather than the final root cause.

solution.intent: Prevent Calico from displacing the NodeLocal DNS iptables rules by changing the Felix chain insertion mode to Append.
solution.concrete_example: Add chainInsertMode: Append to the FelixConfiguration and confirm that the NodeLocal DNS iptables rules remain installed.

edges.comment: From c11 on the reporter's Calico deployment: the reporter kept this FelixConfiguration change. It restored service accessibility from all nodes and preserved NodeLocal DNS rules, but the DNS timeout volume remained, so it is not the final fix.

solution.intent: Treat the remaining delays as a Calico VXLAN interface offload problem, disable RX and TX offload on vxlan.calico, and retest DNS and netchecker before declaring the incident resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Run `sudo ethtool --offload vxlan.calico rx off tx off` on the affected nodes, then repeat uncached DNS queries through the service IP and the netchecker request to verify that the delays are gone.
solution.inference_hint: The collected evidence localizes the remaining problem to the service/overlay networking path rather than CoreDNS: direct pod-IP queries work, service traffic and Calico-to-service traffic time out, and delays persist after correcting the resolver loop and iptables ordering. Mapping the characteristic delay to vxlan.calico offload is the final diagnosis; the reporter validates it by observing that disabling both offloads removes the problem immediately.

edges.comment: Resolution from c11-c12 on the original reporter's Calico cluster: after the resolver-loop and iptables issues were addressed but delays remained, the reporter matched the one-minute behavior to the Calico issue, ran the ethtool command, and explicitly reported that the problem was completely and instantly gone.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause as RX/TX offload on the Calico vxlan.calico interface, not a CoreDNS configuration defect.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the service-path evidence: direct CoreDNS pod-IP queries work, service-IP and Calico API-service traffic time out, and uncached requests exhibit multi-second or approximately one-minute delays.
Must recommend disabling RX and TX offload on vxlan.calico with ethtool.

Must not treat removing the NodeLocal DNS forwarding loop or setting Felix chainInsertMode to Append as the complete fix; both changes addressed real secondary problems, but the timeout symptoms remained.
Must ask the user to retest service-IP DNS queries and the delayed request after changing the offload settings, and only treat the issue as resolved after the user confirms the timeouts are gone.

persona_hint.experience_level: Hands-on Kubernetes operator who can deploy comparison clusters, inspect pod and system logs, edit systemd and kubelet configuration, modify Calico FelixConfiguration, run dig and ethtool, but is uncertain about the deeper DNS and network mechanics.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, candid, and exploratory; posts raw commands and logs, follows leads quickly, acknowledges uncertainty, and reports both partial improvements and remaining symptoms.
